selection.note: Sample IDS are recorded explicitly below. The seed reproduces the draw ONLY if the selection code is byte-identical; it will not be. Use the ids.

power.caveat: In SD units. The SD of top-10 overlap is UNKNOWN until the after-measurement exists, so this cannot yet be expressed in overlap points.

what_this_measures: Top-10 KNN neighbourhood over STORED vectors, before the D-A/D5 re-embed.
This is EMBEDDING DRIFT, not retrieval quality: it needs no ground truth, which is both its virtue and its limit.
It CANNOT distinguish an improvement from a regression on its own. It reports how much moved, and whether Thai moved differently from the corpus.
It does not license any claim in either direction about the Thai U+0E33 decomposition. That remains arguably an improvement and explicitly unmeasured.

Groups B and C exist because after the re-embed EVERYTHING moves (D-A changes 88.99% of names). A Thai-only measurement would show large drift and prove nothing. The question is whether A drifts MORE than B and C.
Raw stored vectors are included so a different metric (e.g. cosine shift) can be computed later; the neighbour lists alone would not permit that.
how_to_compare: Re-run KNN for the SAME ids after the re-embed; compare top-10 overlap per doc; test A vs B and A vs C.
